governing_question: How does Arkansas generate, attract, circulate, retain, invest and compound capital while preserving competitive markets, private initiative, individual liberty and broadening ownership?
central_proposition: Constitutional Capitalism differs from tax-and-spend government and from extraction economies by maximizing productive circulation and beneficial external income while protecting competitive markets—and by refusing to call revenue or profit 'public income' until reserved public cash clears.
organizing_sentence: Money, Markets & Ownership is the economic heart of the unabridged system: the life of an Arkansas dollar, the three economies, revenue and public-income architecture, credit and capital formation, ownership by function, competitive markets, external income, and Geographic Money Statements—without inventing COUNTABLE dollars.

arkansas_dollar_lifecycle.title: The Arkansas Dollar
arkansas_dollar_lifecycle.objective: Maximize productive circulation and beneficial external income while distinguishing healthy trade from structural extraction.
arkansas_dollar_lifecycle.not: Keeping every dollar inside Arkansas (neither realistic nor desirable).

distinctions.question: What Arkansas receives relative to what leaves—and whether relationships build or diminish productive capacity.

three_economies.title: Three Economies
three_economies.rule: A healthy system does not allow any one economy to feed indefinitely upon the others. All three should contribute to productive capacity and household prosperity.

revenue_taxonomy.title: Tax and revenue architecture
revenue_taxonomy.long_term_objective: Reduce/eliminate dependence on personal income tax and property tax only when replacement capacity exists.
revenue_taxonomy.dependency_rule: Dependency Rule governs everything — no abolish-today.

public_income_firewall.title: Public income versus taxation
public_income_firewall.distinction: Government normally finances itself by taking a portion of economic activity after it occurs. CC asks whether some public revenue can arise because the public possesses an economically productive claim.
firewall: Public income is not reserved public cash.
public_income_firewall.countable_rule: COUNTABLE remains $0 until the evidence chain proves otherwise.
public_income_firewall.food_hub_discipline_example: Food-hub work is an example of intellectual discipline—not a failed research project—because COUNTABLE stayed $0 without free cash.

banking_credit.title: Banking, credit and capital formation
questions: Where does the capital ultimately accumulate?
banking_credit.not: Do not let Pass 3.4 spontaneously become a public-bank project.

ownership_architecture.title: Ownership architecture
ownership_architecture.not: Private versus public as the only axis
ownership_architecture.principle: Choose ownership structures based on function, incentives, competition, risk and public purpose—not ideological preference for one ownership form.

competitive_markets.title: Competitive markets
competitive_markets.definition: Markets are information and coordination systems.
competitive_markets.state_objective: Not to replace markets—to design and protect conditions under which markets remain markets.
competitive_markets.capitalism_in_cc: This is a core explanation of Capitalism in Constitutional Capitalism.
competitive_markets.contradiction: CX-M21-02 state antitrust vs federal preemption → STAGE_4

extraction_test.title: Extraction Test
extraction_test.precision_rule: Precision rather than anti-corporate rhetoric. Large firms can create productivity, employment, technology, and market access.
extraction_test.concern: When scale allows rents or political/economic control inconsistent with competitive markets.
questions: Does the relationship increase Arkansas productive capacity?
Does political influence distort the rules?
extraction_test.use: Evaluate relationships rather than labeling firms good or bad.

external_income.title: External income
external_income.insight: Arkansas cannot become wealthier merely by circulating the same internal dollar faster.

distinction.external_revenue: Money entering Arkansas from outside demand
distinction.external_capital_ownership: Who owns the surplus and assets that produce that revenue

external_income.factory_note: A factory can bring revenue into Arkansas while simultaneously exporting much of its surplus. Both sides belong in the ledger.

bound_scales.label: Tourism visitor spend (impact report)
bound_scales.note: Scale anchor — not COUNTABLE public income

productive_retention.title: Arkansas capital retention — productive retention
productive_retention.rule: Arkansas should happily send money elsewhere when the exchange produces greater value.
productive_retention.problem: Whether Arkansas systematically consumes externally owned goods/services while failing to build assets and export valuable production of its own.
productive_retention.definition: Productive retention rather than simplistic buy-local.

integration_spine.title: Economic heart of Constitutional Capitalism
integration_spine.while: Government protects competitive markets and democratic institutions prevent accumulated capital from purchasing the rules.

counterarguments.claim: Public enterprises crowd out private firms.
counterarguments.strong_form: State ownership displaces private investment and innovation.
counterarguments.architecture_answer: Ownership chosen by function; markets remain primary coordination systems; public income requires waterfall discipline and competition protection—not blanket nationalization.
counterarguments.unresolved: STAGE_4 crowding studies by sector (often via 3.6)

counterarguments.claim: Government cannot competently own productive assets.
counterarguments.strong_form: Public ownership always underperforms and becomes patronage.
counterarguments.architecture_answer: Firewall and waterfall force transparent cost/reserve/distributable cash. Incompetent claims without reserved cash cannot become COUNTABLE. Patronage is a Stage 4/3.5 attack surface.

counterarguments.claim: Eliminating income/property taxes creates regressive replacements.
counterarguments.strong_form: Any replacement stack hits poor households harder.
counterarguments.architecture_answer: Dependency Rule forbids abolish-today. Classification axes include progressivity and household incidence. Residual wealth contribution is last resort on substantial surplus—not ordinary wages.

counterarguments.strong_form: Buy-local is autarky that shrinks welfare.
counterarguments.architecture_answer: Productive retention—not autarky. Happy to send money out when exchange produces greater value.

counterarguments.strong_form: Prosperity Fund is a slush fund.
counterarguments.architecture_answer: Ring-fence, published ledgers, reserved-cash gates, and power firewall are architectural answers; adversarial capture testing is Stage 4/3.5.

counterarguments.claim: Broad ownership sacrifices economies of scale.
counterarguments.architecture_answer: Ownership spectrum allows scale where function requires it; Extraction Test evaluates concentration effects without banning scale.

counterarguments.strong_form: Any public claim or competition rule drives investment out.
counterarguments.architecture_answer: External investment is not automatically extraction; healthy outside capital welcome. Rules aim at competitive markets and proportionate public return—not capital hostility.

counterarguments.claim: Arkansas cannot affect monopoly power governed federally.
counterarguments.strong_form: State antitrust is preempted; local action is theater.
counterarguments.architecture_answer: CX-M21-02 remains OPEN_ASSIGNED Stage 4. Architecture still designs market conditions Arkansas can lawfully affect (procurement, licensing, public options, disclosure).

counterarguments.claim: Government investment socializes losses while politicians claim successes.
counterarguments.strong_form: Heads I win, tails taxpayers lose.
counterarguments.architecture_answer: Waterfall requires operating costs and reserves before distributable surplus; COUNTABLE forbids claiming success as cash before reserved public cash exists.

counterarguments.claim: Public income is too volatile / becomes a slush fund.
counterarguments.strong_form: Enterprise revenue swings destroy budgets; funds get raided.
counterarguments.architecture_answer: Classification axes include volatility and stability; Dependency Rule keeps bridges; ring-fence and reserves are required before tax retirement.

open_validation_questions.question: When can any public-income engine promote COUNTABLE reserved cash under recession and incidence stress?
What is Arkansas's lawful reach on concentrated markets given federal antitrust preemption?
Can a county Geographic Money Statement be populated without fabricating ownership geography from SOD deposits?
What household incidence results from each major replacement-stack feeder?
Does Arkansas need a public bank, or do existing authorities + CDFIs + ring-fenced funds suffice?
How should federal transfer volatility be modeled in Dependency Rule sequencing?
